newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares up on mill privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares up on mill privatisation.

text.p: A privatisation in the milling sector boosted Egyptian share prices, which rose for the fourth consecutive trading day on Thursday and brokers said they expected the market to trade up in the coming week.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all share index closed 2.39 points higher at 351.75 points. Turnover was 178.9 million pounds ($52.7 million).

The Egyptian state sold on Thursday 1.176 million shares equivalent to 29.4 percent in Alexandria Flour Mills as part of its privatisation programme, the CMA said. It said the shares were sold for 97.02 million pounds, or 82.5 pounds per share.

The state had offered investors 30 percent or 1.2 million shares of the mill's total four million shares at an initial price of 75 pounds per share. The state also sold an additional 10 percent to the miller's workers.

Officials at the Commercial International Investment Company, one of the agents for the sale, said the offer had been about 20 times oversubscribed. They said they did not know why the remaining 24,000 shares were not sold on Thursday and they expected the state to sell them on Sunday.
The London-based brokers T. Hoare and Co. said on Tuesday that it was the best-valued stock in the milling sector. It had recommended investors buy the stock at up to 85 pounds.

"I expect to see investable cash spill into some of the other mills," said Tareq Lotfy of Intercapital. He said he also expected the Alexandria privatisation to touch off a more active secondary market and saw a trend where institutional investors would start to diversify their holdings.

Upper Egypt Flour Mills traded 3.86 million pounds with its share closing up 0.98 at 78.98. General Silos and Storage closed a fraction lower, down 0.01 at 87 in trade worth 2.8 million, the CMA statement said.
As the end of the financial year on June 30 approached, companies had been cashing in their gains.
"There were a lot of sellers in the past period and retailers were getting out of the market before the end of the financial year in June," said Sherif Cararah of brokers EFG-Hermes. "
The index for openly traded firms fell to 473.45 from 475.89 and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms gained slightly to 262.38 from 259.07.
Of the 90 shares traded, 37 rose, 33 fell while 20 ended unchanged, the CMA said.
